newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BOLSWESSANEN TO MOVE FINANCE UNIT FROM BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: BOLSWESSANEN TO MOVE FINANCE UNIT FROM BELGIUM.

text.p: Dutch food and drinks group Koninklijke Bolswessanen NV plans to move its Belgian corporate finance centre back to the Netherlands at the end of June, the company said on Thursday.
"Our coordination center is going to back to (our Dutch headquarters) in Amstelveen," a Bolswessanen spokeswoman in the group's Dutch headquarters told Reuters.
"The fiscal advantages that are offered in Belgium have now also become available in the Netherlands," she added.
Earlier on Thursday, Dutch chemicals group DSM said it would move its Belgian finance activity to the Netherlands.
"The changes in the corporate tax law from January 1, 1997 for business activities in the Netherlands have resulted in this decision," DSM said in a statement.
Last year, the Dutch government passed a new corporate tax law, effective from 1997, aimed at enticing foreign-based financing units of Dutch companies back to the Netherlands.

Belgian tax officials say the law was aimed mainly at Belgium's so-called "coordination centres", which are corporate finance centres who serve the various units of large companies and enjoy low tax rates, notably on intragroup lending.
Bolswessanen's Belgian coordination centre in Antwerp was set up six years ago and employs 11 people. "Most of these jobs will disappear," a Belgian source told Reuters.
The 20 staff employed at DSM Intra Services NV in Genk, Belgium, will be transferred to Heerlen in the Netherlands.
